firm.label: Firm
firm.about: Fixed by records from outside the Bible (Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Greek or Roman).

close.label: Close
close.about: Most scholars agree to within a few years.

debated.label: Debated
debated.about: Scholars hold clearly different dates. Psalt shows the traditional one.

estimate.label: Estimate
estimate.about: Counted back from the Bible's own numbers; there is no outside record to check it against.

undated.label: Undated
undated.about: The Bible gives no date that can be placed on a calendar.

eras.name: Beginnings
eras.summary: Creation, the fall, the flood and the tower of Babel: the world before Abraham.

eras.name: The Patriarchs
eras.summary: God's promise to Abraham, passed down through Isaac, Jacob and the twelve tribes.

events.name: Abram is called to leave Haran
events.basis: Counted back from the Exodus using the years given in Genesis and Exodus.

events.name: God's covenant with Abraham
events.basis: Counted back from the Exodus using the years given in Genesis and Exodus.

events.name: Isaac is born
events.basis: Abraham was 100 (Genesis 21:5); counted back from the Exodus.

events.name: Jacob and Esau are born
events.basis: Isaac was 60 (Genesis 25:26); counted back from the Exodus.

events.name: Joseph is sold into Egypt
events.basis: Counted back from the Exodus using the years in Genesis.

events.name: Jacob's family moves to Egypt
events.basis: 430 years before the Exodus (Exodus 12:40).

books.note: Often set in this period; its date is uncertain

eras.name: Exodus and Wilderness
eras.summary: Israel leaves Egypt, receives the law at Sinai, and wanders forty years in the wilderness.

events.name: Moses is born
events.basis: 80 years before the Exodus (Exodus 7:7), so it moves with the Exodus date.

events.name: The burning bush
events.basis: Depends on the Exodus date.

events.name: The Passover
events.basis: Depends on the Exodus date.

events.name: Crossing the Red Sea
events.basis: The Exodus is dated c. 1446 BC (from 1 Kings 6:1) or c. 1260 BC (from archaeology). Both views have scholarly support.

events.name: The Ten Commandments at Sinai
events.basis: Depends on the Exodus date.

events.name: The twelve spies
events.basis: Depends on the Exodus date.

events.name: Moses dies on Mount Nebo
events.basis: Forty years after the Exodus, so it moves with the Exodus date.

eras.name: Conquest and Judges
eras.summary: Israel enters Canaan under Joshua, then is led by judges in a cycle of falling away and rescue.

events.name: Israel crosses the Jordan
events.basis: Depends on the Exodus date.

events.name: The walls of Jericho fall
events.basis: Depends on the Exodus date; the archaeology of Jericho is also debated.

events.name: Deborah and Barak
events.basis: The judges overlap and their years are hard to place; this is a rough estimate.

events.name: Gideon
events.basis: The judges overlap and their years are hard to place; this is a rough estimate.

events.name: Ruth and Naomi
events.basis: "In the days when the judges ruled" (Ruth 1:1); no closer date is given.

events.name: Samson
events.basis: The judges overlap and their years are hard to place; this is a rough estimate.

eras.name: The United Kingdom
eras.summary: Israel asks for a king. Saul, David and Solomon reign, and the Temple is built in Jerusalem.

events.name: Samuel anoints Saul
events.basis: The length of Saul's reign is unclear in the Hebrew text of 1 Samuel 13:1.

events.name: David and Goliath
events.basis: Placed in Saul's reign, whose length is uncertain.

events.name: David becomes king
events.basis: Counted back from Solomon's reign; most scholars place it within a few years of 1010 BC.

events.name: David takes Jerusalem
events.basis: Seven and a half years into his reign (2 Samuel 5:5).

events.name: Solomon becomes king
events.basis: Counted back from the division of the kingdom; scholars differ by a few years.

events.name: Solomon builds the Temple
events.basis: Begun in the fourth year of his reign and finished seven years later (1 Kings 6:1, 38).

books.note: Many psalms are attributed to David

eras.name: The Divided Kingdom
eras.summary: The kingdom splits into Israel and Judah. Prophets call both back to God until Assyria and Babylon conquer them.

events.name: The kingdom splits in two
events.basis: Scholars place it between about 931 and 922 BC.

events.name: Elijah on Mount Carmel
events.basis: During Ahab's reign; Assyrian records name Ahab at the battle of Qarqar in 853 BC.

events.name: Jonah goes to Nineveh
events.basis: Jonah lived under Jeroboam II, c. 793–753 BC (2 Kings 14:25).

events.name: Isaiah's vision in the Temple
events.basis: "In the year that king Uzziah died" (Isaiah 6:1), about 740 BC.

events.name: Assyria takes Samaria
events.basis: Recorded by the Assyrian kings Shalmaneser V and Sargon II.

events.name: Hezekiah and Sennacherib
events.basis: Recorded in Sennacherib's own annals.

events.name: Josiah finds the book of the law
events.basis: In Josiah's 18th year (2 Kings 22:3), dated by the kings of Judah.

events.name: Babylon destroys Jerusalem
events.basis: Babylonian records fix the period; scholars differ on which of the two years.

eras.name: Exile and Return
eras.summary: Judah lives in exile in Babylon, then returns under Persian rule to rebuild the Temple and the walls of Jerusalem.

events.name: Daniel is taken to Babylon
events.basis: The Babylonian Chronicle records Nebuchadnezzar's campaign of 605 BC.

events.name: Ezekiel's vision by the river
events.basis: In the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity (Ezekiel 1:2), which began in 597 BC.

events.name: Daniel in the lions' den
events.basis: After Babylon fell in 539 BC, but who "Darius the Mede" was is debated.

events.name: Cyrus lets the exiles return
events.basis: The first year of Cyrus as king of Babylon (Ezra 1:1), fixed by Persian chronology.

events.name: The Temple is rebuilt
events.basis: The sixth year of king Darius I (Ezra 6:15), fixed by Persian chronology.

events.name: Esther becomes queen
events.basis: The seventh year of Ahasuerus (Esther 2:16), usually identified as Xerxes I.

events.name: Ezra returns to Jerusalem
events.basis: The seventh year of Artaxerxes (Ezra 7:7): 458 BC for Artaxerxes I, but some scholars argue for 398 BC.

events.name: Nehemiah rebuilds the walls
events.basis: The 20th year of Artaxerxes I (Nehemiah 2:1), fixed by Persian chronology.

eras.name: Between the Testaments
eras.summary: About four centuries with no books in the Protestant Bible. Greek and then Roman rule shape the world Jesus is born into.

events.name: Alexander the Great conquers the region
events.basis: Recorded by Greek historians.

events.name: The Maccabean revolt
events.basis: Recorded in 1 Maccabees and by Josephus.

events.name: Rome takes Judea
events.basis: Pompey took Jerusalem in 63 BC, recorded by Roman historians and Josephus.

events.name: Herod the Great becomes king
events.basis: Recorded by Josephus and Roman sources.

eras.name: The Life of Jesus
eras.summary: Jesus is born in Bethlehem, teaches and heals in Galilee and Judea, is crucified in Jerusalem and rises again.

events.name: Jesus is born in Bethlehem
events.basis: Before the death of Herod the Great (Matthew 2), which most date to 4 BC.

events.name: Jesus is baptized
events.basis: Around "the fifteenth year of Tiberius" (Luke 3:1); scholars count that year slightly differently.

events.name: The Sermon on the Mount
events.basis: Placed early in the ministry; the Gospels give no year.

events.name: Feeding the five thousand
events.basis: Near a Passover (John 6:4); the exact year is not given.

events.name: The crucifixion
events.basis: Most scholars choose AD 30 or AD 33, both under Pontius Pilate (AD 26–36).

events.name: The resurrection
events.basis: Three days after the crucifixion, so AD 30 or AD 33.

eras.name: The Early Church
eras.summary: The Holy Spirit comes at Pentecost, and the apostles carry the gospel across the Roman world.

events.name: Pentecost
events.basis: Fifty days after the resurrection, so AD 30 or AD 33.

events.name: Saul's conversion on the road to Damascus
events.basis: Scholars place it within a few years of AD 34.

events.name: Paul's first journey
events.basis: Dated from the later anchor of Gallio in Corinth (Acts 18:12), known from an inscription found at Delphi.

events.name: The council at Jerusalem
events.basis: Dated from the Gallio inscription at Delphi.

events.name: Paul reaches Rome
events.basis: After the change of governors from Felix to Festus (Acts 24:27), around AD 59–60.

events.name: Romans destroy the Temple
events.basis: Recorded by Josephus and Roman historians.

events.name: Revelation is written on Patmos
events.basis: Most date it c. AD 95 under Domitian; some argue for before AD 70.
